brief: Push A is next, today 26 November. Legs B on 25 November went well, and you trained it at full weights, three sets each, not the lighter-week numbers on the card (140, 120, 160 and so on): barbell RDL 185 for 10, 10, 10, leg extension 157.5 for 12 on all three, leg press 200 for 12 on all three, leg curl 157.5 for 12 on all three, calf press 300 for 15, 15, 12, ab machine 70 for 10 on all three, ab wheel 10 and 10, 52 minutes. Every lift is at or above 14 November. I do not know whether you saw the lighter card or chose to go heavy; either way you had no training from 18 to 22 November and the night went up, not down, so the lighter week is not doing a job. One caveat: that is one lower-body night, and tonight is your first upper-body night in 11 days. The calendar still calls 25 November to 1 December a lighter week and I cannot change the calendar, but I am putting the weights back at what you have already lifted at this gym, nothing above proven work except one earned notch on the crossover. The app still holds every card this week to two sets a lift (its lighter-week set budget, which I cannot change), so tonight's card shows two sets; do more if you want to, the log is what I read. One change to the program, version 18: calves get a second lift. Single-leg dumbbell calf raise off a step, right after the calf press and ahead of the ab work (I moved both calf lifts up so they are not the slots that get dropped late), two sets of 12 to 15 (one set means both legs, weaker first, logged as one row), so calves go from 6 direct sets a week to 8. I should not have held calves waiting for your answer: your gym file already lists dumbbells and step platforms, and your only calf note, from 30 July, was a question, not a limit. Tonight's Push A, two sets each on the card: Smith incline 180 for 7; chest press 165 for 10 (you did 165 for 10 on Push B on 23 November; Push B's chest press next asks 172.5 for 8, the two days differ because Push A is the 10 to 12 day and Push B the 8 to 10 day); low-to-high crossover 13.75 for 12 (12.5 plus one 1.25 lb add-on weight); lateral raise 17.5 for 14 (you asked on 23 November why four sets for a small muscle: side delts are scored on stage and sit at the bottom of their range, and the four-set slot is the first thing I look at again on 2 December); chest dip bodyweight 13; lying plate neck flexion 5 lb for 15 for one set, the first time it has ever been done, so the 5 is my choice, not a measured number, and flexion is normally the weaker side. Next Legs B the numbers go up: RDL 195 for 8, leg extension 165 for 10, leg press 220 for 10, leg curl 165 for 10; calf press holds 300 until all three sets reach 15. Dates: assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December, show 1 March, 95 days away. What I still need: a morning bodyweight (nothing logged since 23 August, 207 lb, 95 days; the Bodyweight button on the workout screen), and your division.

block.why: Today, 26 November, the calendar is in its lighter week (25 November to 1 December), then assessment 2 to 8 December and prep from 9 December; the show is 95 days away. The new fact since the 25 November packet is the Legs B night of 25 November: it was logged at full weights and three sets, not the lighter card, and every lift was at or above 14 November (RDL 185 for 10, 10, 10 after 9, 9, 9; leg extension, leg press and leg curl 12, 12, 12 at their old weights; calf press 300 for 15, 15, 12; ab machine 70 for 10 on all three; 52 minutes). Before that there was no training from 18 to 22 November and only Push B and Pull B on 23 and 24 November, so the nine days in a row of 9 to 17 November, which the lighter week was meant to pay for, were already followed by five days off. I do not know whether you saw the lighter card; the night shows the work is being recovered from, so the review reverses its 25 November call to leave the cards lighter, and the fact that changes it is the 25 November log. Cards for the rest of this week carry weights you have already lifted at this gym, with no step above proven work, instead of weights about 20 percent lighter; the app still holds each card to two sets in this week (its lighter-week set budget, which the validator showed me and I cannot change), so this week is fewer sets at real weights. The calendar label does not change, and that is not mine to edit. Program change today: version 18 adds a second calf lift (single-leg dumbbell calf raise, Legs B, 2 sets), because calves are scored on stage and I had held them for an answer that the gym file already gives. Programming still to decide has a date: side delts on 2 December. Honest limit: every card this week is held to two sets, so tonight's Push A and Push B on or about 29 November cannot show whether a fourth lateral set gets done; 2 December is the first day after the lighter week and the 14-day guard, not new evidence. Loads to run into assessment (the reversal rests on Legs B alone; if tonight's Push A falls below 15 November, that is the signal): smith incline 180, chest press 165, row 60 for 10, close pulldown 135, shrug 80 for 18, lateral raise 17.5, RDL 185 for 10, leg press 200 for 12, leg extension and leg curl 157.5 for 12, calf press 300, shoulder press 50.

Push B on 23 November: chest press 165 for 10, 10, 10, the top of Push B's 8 to 10 on every set, up from 165 for 9 on 12 November, and high-to-low crossover 30.5 for 15, 15. Push A lifts repeat from 15 November: chest press 157.5 for 12, 12, 12, smith incline 180 for 6, 7, 8, low-to-high crossover 12.5 for 15 on all three. All going up at this gym. Sets hold; the weights move. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 18 planned a week, of which 18 are direct sets; 10.3 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

Eight are the two presses that lead each push day (smith incline 4, shoulder press 4); seven are half credit from the chest press, crossovers and dips. No set is in the week only for front delts, so the only way to lower this is to cut chest or shoulder pressing, and neither should be cut. Shoulder press 50 for 10 on all four sets on 23 November, the first time the top of the range was hit on every set; smith incline 180 for 6, 7, 8 on 15 November. Hold. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 15 planned a week, of which 8 are direct sets; 9.1 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

side-delts.why: Raised on 18 November (version 14). Side delts decide how wide the shoulders look on stage; they had the smallest share of any scored muscle (6 direct sets, 8 counted, against 15.5 for rear delts), so lateral raises went to four sets on each push day: 8 direct, 10 counted with half credit from the shoulder press, the bottom of the 10 to 20 range. First four-set night, 23 November on Push B: 17.5 for 13, 13, 13 and the fourth set was not done, and you asked why four sets for a small muscle. The honest count: the 6.3 a week done is an average over weeks that include rest days and a partial week (the week of 17 to 22 November had no push night) and mostly predate the four-set cards, so it does not prove the fourth set is the problem; there has been exactly one four-set night and three of four sets were done. Direct sets are now 8 against the rear delts' 7; on the counted number it is 10 against 12.5. 15 November on Push A was 17.5 for 12, 12, 12 (three sets, before the fourth existed). The weight is right (17.5, up from 15). The decision between a third lateral day and a second side-delt lift stays with the review of 2 December: the lighter week (25 November to 2 December) cuts sets and is a poor week to add a day, and adding a day now would walk back the 14 November removal of the Pull A cable lateral raise (version 12) inside the 14-day guard. Honest limit on the date: the lighter week runs about 60 percent of the sets at lighter weights, so its Push A cannot show whether a fourth lateral set at 17.5 works. What 2 December adds is calendar, not new evidence: it is the first review after the lighter week ends (1 December is its last day), and the decision (a third lateral day or a second side-delt lift) is made then on the 23 November night and whatever Push A shows. Until then side delts stay at 8 direct, 10 counted, the floor of their range. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 10 planned a week, of which 8 are direct sets; 6.3 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

The dose-response research (roughly 10 to 20 hard sets per muscle a week, Schoenfeld, Ogborn and Krieger 2017) puts 18 inside the range, and the row keeps adding load at every visit, so the four stay; a note on the card changes that. Both rows are going up: seated row 112.5 for 10 on all four on 16 November, chest-supported row 60 for 10 on all four on 24 November (9 on 13 November). Hold. prep.plan: Thirteen days come before prep (from 26 November). The build block ended on 24 November. The calendar calls 25 November to 1 December a lighter week; the app holds each card to two sets, and I have the weights at what you have already lifted, because the 25 November Legs B went up, not down (see the block). The week of 2 December is assessment: each main lift is run at its current weight for its best reps, and the starting bodyweight is set. Prep starts on 9 December and runs just under 12 weeks. Weeks 1 to 4 (9 December to 5 January): the same lifts and weights as now, with the sets as they stand after the side-delt decision (1 December review) and the second calf lift added on 26 November; in prep, holding reps at the same weight while bodyweight comes down is the win. Weeks 5 to 8 (6 January to 2 February): the weights stay, and if recovery slips, sets come off what the stage scores least (rear delts, forearms, traps, the hip machines) before anything comes off side delts, back, chest, arms, quads or calves. Weeks 9 to 11 (3 to 21 February): the same, no new lifts, no set taken to a grinding rep. The final week (22 February to 1 March): about half the sets, with the last hard leg session early in the week. Fat loss is paced at about half a percent to one percent of bodyweight a week, which at your last logged 207 lb is about 1 to 2 lb a week. It is checked by the weekly average of morning weigh-ins: less than half a percent for two weeks running means food or daily walking has to change; more than one percent with reps dropping means it is too fast. From 9 December to the show is just under 12 weeks, so at that pace the most that can come off is roughly 12 to 23 lb from 207. Whether that is enough is not something I can tell: the last weigh-in in the log is 23 August, and there are no photos and no division. If more than that has to come off, the only slack is the 14 days before 9 December, which is why the weigh-in matters now and not in December. The prep phase in the calendar is a placeholder that detailed programming replaces at assessment, so this plan is a default, not a decision. What it protects, in order, once real data arrives: side delts, upper chest (Push A), back, arms, quads, calves; the deadlift and RDL are climbing 5 to 10 lb a visit now (deadlift 250 for 5 on 16 November) and in a deficit they hold their weight rather than climb. If no bodyweight arrives by 2 December, I will start prep on 9 December from 207 lb (23 August) and say so. Assessment (2 to 8 December) reads each main lift at its current weight for its best reps; if two of them come in under their reps of 15 to 25 November, prep starts with sets coming off the least-scored muscles at once, not in week 5. In prep, a cut in sets is triggered by any week where two or more main lifts fall below their previous reps or where a session ends with its late slots skipped.

changes_today.why: Calves are scored on stage and sit at 6 direct sets a week (9 counted, floor 8), all of them the calf press on the leg press, 3 on each leg day. The 17 and 25 November nights show the lift is working and the sets get done (300 for 13, 13, 13 on 17 November; 300 for 15, 15, 12 on 25 November, the top of 12 to 15), so the missing piece is volume and a second angle, not a heavier press. On 19 November I asked whether your gym has a calf machine and the 23 July photos answered it (none; leg press only); the 25 November packet then held calves for an answer on a second lift and said I would not go past three sets a day on my own. That was wrong twice: your gym file already lists dumbbells and step platforms, so single-leg dumbbell calf raises are programmable without asking, and your only calf note (30 July, Why four sets) was a question, not a limit. So the second lift goes in today: single-leg dumbbell calf raise off a step, straight after the calf press and ahead of the ab work, 2 sets of 12 to 15, where one set means both legs (weaker leg first, then the other) logged as one row, 60 seconds between sets. Calves go from 6 direct to 8 and from 9 counted to 11, inside 8 to 16. Legs B goes from 20 to 22 sets. Two sets, not three: Legs B ran 52 minutes on 25 November and your cards lose their late slots when nights run long, which is why it now sits ahead of the ab work, not after it, so the new lift starts small; if both sets get done for two Legs B nights, a third is the next question. The 30 on the card is my starting guess for one dumbbell, not a measured number: you have never logged this lift. Pick the weight where 12 is hard on your weaker leg and the card learns from that.

Calves are scored on stage and the abs are not. The calf press was 7th on Legs B and the new single-leg calf raise would have been 8th behind five ab sets, on the night type where late slots get dropped (30 October, 22 sets in 29 minutes). Both calf lifts now come right after the leg curl, ahead of the ab wheel and ab machine. No sets change.
